- Root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is purity, clarity, and freedom from admixture; the essence of a thing being unmixed with anything foreign.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance is the purification of intention (niyyah) and action (ʿamal) from any motive other than seeking Allah's Face (wajh Allāh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the purity of gold or honey; metaphorical (majāz) usage refers to the heart's purity from hypocrisy (riyāʾ) and showing-off.
- Root: ن-و-ي (n-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is intent, purpose, and resolve; the heart's determination towards a goal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance is the heart's resolve (qaṣd) which distinguishes acts of worship (ʿibādāt) from mere habits (ʿādāt), making them valid (ṣaḥīḥ) before Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is the physical direction of travel; metaphorical usage is the spiritual direction of the heart's aim.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is truthfulness, veracity, and strength in speech and action; the opposite of falsehood (kidhb).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance is the alignment of the inner (sirr) and outer (ʿalāniyyah) states of a person, making their faith (īmān) firm.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is truthful speech; metaphorical usage is the strength of a spear (ṣidq al-sanān) and the firmness of resolve.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ḥaṣr (Restriction) via "Innamā" (إنما). The particle "innamā" is used for restriction, affirming the mentioned thing (al-madhkūr) and negating everything else (nafy mā ʿadāhu). This is syntactically crucial for understanding the Hadith "Innamā al-aʿmālu bil-niyyāt" — actions are only valid through intention, negating the validity of actions performed without it.
chapters.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless our Master Muḥammad, his family, and his companions and grant them peace. Praise be to Allah, the One, the Subduer (al-Qahhār), the Mighty, the Forgiving (al-Ghaffār), the Appointer of destinies (muqaddir al-aqdār), the Disposer of all affairs, who wraps the night over the day — a lesson for those possessed of hearts and eyesights. He is the One who awakened from His creation whom He chose, admitting him into the company of the righteous (al-akhyār); He granted success to whom He selected from His servants, making him among the pious (al-abrār); He gave insight to those He loves regarding the realities (al-ḥaqāʾiq), so they became ascetic (zahidū) in this abode. They strove for His pleasure and prepared for the Abode of Permanence (dār al-qarār), avoiding what incurs His wrath and fearing the punishment of the Fire.

I praise Him with praise for all His blessings, and I ask Him for increase from His bounty and generosity. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, in acknowledgment of His Oneness (waḥdāniyyah) and in recognition of what is obligatory upon all creation of submission to His Lordship (rubūbiyyah). I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant, His Messenger, His beloved, the Chosen One from His creation, and the most noble of the first and the last from His creatures — the most noble of creation, the most pure, the most complete, the most knowledgeable of Allah, the most fearful of Him, the most learned of Him, the most God-fearing, the most diligent in striving, worship, fear, and asceticism, the greatest in character, and the most kind and gentle with the believers. May Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, upon the Prophets, upon the families of each, and upon all their companions, and upon those who follow them in excellence until the Day of Judgment, whenever the rememberers remember him and whenever the heedless neglect his remembrance.

To proceed: Know that this world (al-dunyā) is an abode of passing away (dār nafād), not an abode of permanence (dār ikhlād); an abode of transit (dār ʿubūr), not an abode of joy (dār ḥubūr); an abode of annihilation (dār fanāʾ), not an abode of endurance (dār baqāʾ); an abode of termination (dār inṣirām), not an abode of continuance (dār dawām). The decisive proofs of transmitted texts (al-nuqūl) and the sound intellects (ṣaḥāʾiḥ al-ʿuqūl) have concurred upon what I have mentioned. This is a matter in which the elite and the commoners, the rich and the rabble, are equal in knowledge, and sense-perception and ocular vision have decreed it, such that no clarity remains for any increase in gnosis (ʿirfān):

*"And nothing is sound in the ears... when the day itself needs a proof."*

Since the world is in the state I described and the admonition I presented, there has come in the Mighty Qurʾān a warning against leaning towards it (al-rukuūn ilayhā), being deluded by it (al-ightirār bihā), and relying upon it — a warning too well-known to be mentioned and too famous to be publicized. Likewise, the Prophetic hadiths and the wise traditions (al-āthār al-ḥikmiyyah) have come. For this reason, the most awakened of its people are the worshippers (al-ʿubbād), and the most intelligent of people regarding it are the ascetics (al-zuhhād). How excellent is what the poet said in describing it:

*"Look at the ruins, how they have changed... after their inhabitants, and how they have become unrecognizable.*
*The calamity dragged its trains over their traces... so their stones fell and broke apart.*
*The community of its people went on their way... and their news vanished and became unknown.*
*When I looked, reflecting upon their abodes... my eyelids poured forth tears that streamed down.*
*Had I been intelligent, I would have desisted from weeping... sufficient for me there is what my eye has beheld.*
*The world set up for us the embellishments of its beauty... as a deception against us and a trick that never tires.*
*It is that which never remained sweet for any taster... except its taste changed and became bitter.*
*A deceiver with its beauty when it advances... a destroyer with its passing when it retreats.*
*A giver that robs its own gifts... a seeker of the ruin of what it has built.*
*And when it builds a matter for a wealthy man... it sets up its siege engines against him and destroys him."*

And another said:

*"And whoever praises the world for an easy life... soon, by my life, he will blame it.*
*When it turns away, it is a regret upon a man... and when it advances, its worries are many."*

Now that what I have mentioned is known and what I have described is established, it is incumbent upon a person to traverse the path of the intelligent and follow the way of the insightful. So we ask Allah, the Generous, the Kind, the Merciful, to bestow this upon us and to guide us to the most upright paths. I am now commencing the compilation of a book that will clarify the path I have presented and serve as a way to adorn oneself with the noble character traits I have described. In it, Allah willing, I will mention a collection of precious subtleties (nafāʾis al-laṭāʾif) and realities of gnosis (ḥaqāʾiq al-maʿārif). I will present what I mention in prose so that it may be further from boredom for the reader and closer to remembrance. I will not commit myself to arranging it into chapters, for that brings boredom to the reader of the book. In it, Allah willing, I will mention noble verses (āyāt karīmāt), Prophetic hadiths, illuminating sayings of the Salaf, and choice transmitted accounts from the righteous — including precious stories and commendable ascetic poetry. In most instances, I will clarify the authenticity (ṣiḥḥah) and excellence (ḥusn) of the hadiths, the status of their transmission (riwāyah), and the explanation of what is hidden and problematic in their meanings. I will also precisely record what needs restriction, guarding against textual corruption (taṣḥīf) and fleeing from alteration (taghyīr) and distortion (taḥrīf).

Then, I will mention it with my chain of transmission (isnād) for it, as this is more impactful upon the souls of its readers. I may omit the chain for brevity and out of fear of prolixity and excess, and because this book is intended for worshippers (al-mutaʿabbidīn) who have no need for knowledge of chains — indeed, they mostly dislike it due to the boredom it causes them. Most of what I mention is from what I narrate, by Allah's praise and bounty, through well-known, famous chains from apparent, widely-circulated, and known books. If there is in a hadith or story a linguistic word or the name of a person, I will restrict and clarify it with precise control and perfect it. What needs explanation, I will explain; what is susceptible to error in its meaning, I will clarify.

There will be included within this book, Allah willing, various types of religious sciences, a collection of its hadith-related, jurisprudential, and religious etiquettes, a portion of the science of hadith and the subtle points of jurisprudence, important matters from the principles of creed (uṣūl al-ʿaqāʾid), precious gems of rules, and subtle wonders that are deemed commendable in what is mentioned and recommended to be mentioned in gatherings. Also included are the gnosis of hearts, their diseases, their medicine, and their treatment. Perhaps something will arise that requires expansion beyond what this book can bear, so I will mention its objective briefly, or I will refer the expansion of its explanation to a book by one of the scholars of insight and intellect. Perhaps I will refer it to a book I myself have authored. I do not intend by this, Allah willing, self-aggrandizement or pride, nor the display of works and their abundance, but rather guidance towards good and indication of it, and clarification of where it is sought and direction to it. I have only alerted to this subtle point because I have seen among people those who criticize the follower of this path — due to their ignorance, evil suspicion, corruption, envy, deficiency, and obstinacy. I wanted this meaning to be established in the mind of the reader of this work, and for him to purify himself from corrupt suspicion and reproach.

I ask Allah, the Generous, for success in good intentions, assistance in all types of acts of obedience, their facilitation, and guidance towards them, continuously increasing until death. I ask Him for that for all whom I love and who love me for Allah's sake, and for the rest of the Muslim men and women. I ask that He gather us and them in the Abode of His Generosity in the highest stations, and that He grant us His pleasure and all aspects of goodness. I have sought refuge in Allah, I have sought aid from Allah, I have placed my trust in Allah. There is no might and no power except with Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. O Allah, I ask You by every means, and I intercede with You by every intercessor, that You benefit me, my loved ones, and all Muslims through this book with a general, far-reaching benefit. O He whom nothing incapacitates, and for whom no matter is too great. And this is the time of my commencement upon the objective of the book.

**Chapter on Sincerity (al-Ikhlāṣ) and Bringing the Intention (al-Niyyah) to Mind in All Outward and Inward Actions**

Allah the Exalted said: {«وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ»} — "And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakah. And that is the correct religion." Its meaning is the upright, straight religion; and it was said: the one that stands with the truth. And Allah knows best.

And He the Exalted said: {«وَمَن يَخْرُجْ مِن بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ»} — "And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah."

And He the Exalted said: {«رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ»} — "Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves."

And He the Exalted said: {«لَن يَنَالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَاؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ التَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ»} — "Never will reach Allah their flesh nor their blood, but it is piety (taqwā) from you that reaches Him."

Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Its meaning is: but it is the intentions (al-niyyāt) from you that reach Him." Ibrāhīm said: "Taqwā is what is intended by it seeking His Face." Imam Abū al-Ḥasan al-Wāḥidī said: al-Zajjāj said: "The meaning is: Allah will not accept the blood and the flesh if they are not accompanied by piety towards Allah the Exalted. He only accepts from you what you guard yourselves with. This is evidence that no act of worship is valid except with intention (niyyah), which is that one intends by it the drawing near to Allah the Exalted and the performance of what He has commanded."

Our Shaykh, the Imam, the Ḥāfiẓ, Abū al-Baqāʾ Khālid ibn Yūsuf ibn Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Mufarrij ibn Bakkār al-Maqdisī al-Nābulusī al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, informed us, saying: Abū al-Yumn al-Kindī informed us; Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī al-Anṣārī informed us; Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Jawharī informed us; Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn al-Muẓaffar al-Ḥāfiẓ informed us; Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Wāsiṭī informed us; Abū Nuʿaym ʿAbd ibn Hishām al-Ḥalabī narrated to us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ al-Laythī, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَىٰ، فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى دُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا أَوِ امْرَأَةٍ يَتَزَوَّجُهَا فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِ»} — "Actions are but by intentions, and every person shall have only what he intended. So whoever's emigration was for Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is for Allah and His Messenger. And whoever's emigration was for a worldly benefit he seeks or a woman he intends to marry, his emigration is for that which he emigrated."

This is a hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon, whose great status and majesty are unanimously acknowledged. It is one of the foundations of faith (qawāʿid al-īmān), its first pillar, and its strongest support. It is a hadith that is solitary (fard) and strange (gharīb) in one respect, and well-known (mashhūr) in another. Its chain revolves around Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī. The Ḥāfiẓ said: "This hadith is not authentic from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, except through ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him; nor from ʿUmar except through ʿAlqamah; nor from ʿAlqamah except through Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Taymī; nor from Muḥammad except through Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd. And from Yaḥyā its narration spread to more than two hundred people, most of them imams." Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ in seven places: at the beginning of his book on Faith (al-Īmān), then in Marriage (al-Nikāḥ), then in Manumission (al-ʿItq), then in Emigration (al-Hijrah), then in Abandoning Deception (Tark al-Ḥiyal), then in Vows (al-Nudhūr). This hadith has been narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ with different wordings: "Actions are but by intentions" (innamā al-aʿmālu bil-niyyāt), and "Actions are but by intention" (innamā al-aʿmālu bil-niyyah). As for what occurs at the beginning of the Book of al-Shihāb — "Actions are by intentions" with the omission of "innamā" — the Ḥāfiẓ Abū Mūsā al-Aṣbahānī said: "The chain of this is not authentic."

As for the meaning of intention (niyyah), it is purpose (qaṣd) and the resolve of the heart (ʿazm al-qalb). The word "innamā" is placed for restriction (al-ḥaṣr), affirming the mentioned thing and negating everything else. So the meaning of the hadith is: religious actions are not valid except with intention. Whoever intends by his emigration the pleasure of Allah the Exalted, then it is for that. And whoever intends by it worldly gain, then that is his share, and he has nothing else.

In this hadith is the stipulation of intention in ablution (wuḍūʾ) and other acts, the ritual bath (ghusl), dry ablution (tayammum), prayer (ṣalāh), alms (zakāh), fasting (ṣawm), seclusion in the mosque (iʿtikāf), pilgrimage (ḥajj), and other acts. Our Imam, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, said: "This hadith enters into seventy chapters of jurisprudence (fiqh)." He also said: "Two-thirds of knowledge enters into this hadith." Abū ʿAbd Allāh Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, said: "One-third of knowledge enters into it." Others have also mentioned the like of this.

The Imam, the Ḥāfiẓ, Abū Bakr al-Bayhaqī said at the beginning of his book Mukhtaṣar al-Sunan, explaining the saying of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, "One-third of knowledge enters into it": "The servant's acquisition (kasb) is only through his heart, his tongue, and his intentions. The intention is one of the divisions of his acquisition, and it is the most preponderant of them, because it is an act of worship by itself, unlike the other two divisions. For speech and action can be corrupted by showing-off (riyāʾ), but intention cannot be corrupted."

The scholars, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them, recommended that compilations be opened with this hadith. Among those who began with it at the start of his book is Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Bukhārī, may Allah have mercy on him, at the beginning of his hadith in his Ṣaḥīḥ, which is the most authentic book after the Book of Allah the Exalted. We have narrated from Imam Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "If I were to compile a book, I would begin every chapter of it with this hadith." We have also narrated from him that he said: "Whoever wants to compile a book should begin it with this hadith."

We have narrated from Imam Abū Sulaymān Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Khaṭṭābī, may Allah have mercy on him, in what I read at the beginning of his book al-Aʿlām fī Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, that he said: "The early scholars among our shaykhs used to recommend presenting the hadith of actions by intention before everything that is initiated and begun from the matters of religion, due to the general need for it in all their types."

And it has reached us from groups of the Salaf, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them, many things of this sort regarding their care for this hadith. And Allah knows best.

Among the things that should be given attention is the clarification of the hadiths that are said to be the foundations of Islam (uṣūl al-Islām), the foundations of the religion (uṣūl al-dīn), or upon which Islam revolves (madār al-Islām), or upon which jurisprudence and knowledge revolve (madār al-fiqh wa-l-ʿilm). We will mention them in this place because one of them is the hadith of actions by intention, and because they are important and should be presented first. The scholars have differed greatly in their number. The Shaykh, the Imam, the Ḥāfiẓ, Abū ʿAmr ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, known as Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, exerted great effort in collecting and clarifying them, and there is no further limit to his verification and mastery. So I will transmit what he mentioned, may Allah have mercy on him, in summary, and I will add to it what is easy for me of what he did not mention. For the religion is sincere advice (al-nuṣḥ). And part of sincere advice is to attribute a benefit that is deemed strange to its originator. Whoever does that is blessed in his knowledge and his state. And whoever implies that, and implies regarding what he takes from the speech of others that it is his own, then he is deserving that he not benefit from his knowledge and that he not be blessed in his state. The people of knowledge and virtue have not ceased to attribute benefits to their originators. We ask Allah the Exalted for success in that always.

The Shaykh Abū ʿAmr, may Allah have mercy on him, said after surveying the statements of the imams regarding the designation of the hadiths upon which Islam revolves, and their disagreement over their exact identities and number, that they reached twenty-six hadiths.

**The First:** The hadith of "Actions are but by intentions."

**The Second:** From ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«مَنْ أَحْدَثَ فِي أَمْرِنَا هَٰذَا مَا لَيْسَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ رَدٌّ»} — "Whoever innovates in this matter of ours that which is not from it, it is rejected." This is a hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon; al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated it in their two Ṣaḥīḥs. In a narration of Muslim: {«مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلًا لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ»} — "Whoever does an action that is not upon our matter, it is rejected." The meaning of "radd" (rejected) is "mardūd" (repudiated), like "khalq" (creation) in the sense of "makhluq" (created thing).

**The Third:** From al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: {«إِنَّ الْحَلَالَ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامَ بَيِّنٌ، وَبَيْنَهُمَا مُشْتَبِهَاتٌ لَا يَعْلَمُهُنَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ، فَمَنِ اتَّقَى الشُّبُهَاتِ اسْتَبْرَأَ لِدِينِهِ وَعِرْضِهِ، وَمَنْ وَقَعَ فِي الشُّبُهَاتِ وَقَعَ فِي الْحَرَامِ، كَالرَّاعِي يَرْعَى حَوْلَ الْحِمَىٰ يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَرْتَعَ فِيهِ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ لِكُلِّ مَلِكٍ حِمًى، أَلَا وَإِنَّ حِمَى اللَّهِ مَحَارِمُهُ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، وَإِذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ»} — "The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters which many people do not know. Whoever guards against the doubtful matters has cleared his religion and his honor, and whoever falls into the doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes around a sanctuary, soon he will graze in it. Indeed, every king has a sanctuary, and indeed, Allah's sanctuary is His prohibitions. Indeed, in the body there is a lump of flesh which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart." This is a hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon; we have narrated it in their two Ṣaḥīḥs. "Yūshiku" is with a ḍammah on the yāʾ and a kasrah on the shīn, meaning "it will soon be."

**The Fourth:** From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and he is the truthful, the believed — narrated to us: {«إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ يُجْمَعُ خَلْقُهُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا نُطْفَةً، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَٰلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَٰلِكَ، ثُمَّ يُرْسَلُ الْمَلَكُ فَيَنْفُخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ وَيُؤْمَرُ بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ: بِكَتْبِ رِزْقِهِ وَأَجَلِهِ وَعَمَلِهِ، وَشَقِيٍّ أَوْ سَعِيدٍ، فَوَالَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ غَيْرُهُ، إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَتَّىٰ مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إِلَّا ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ فَيَدْخُلُهَا، وَإِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ حَتَّىٰ مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إِلَّا ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ فَيَدْخُلُهَا»} — "The creation of each one of you is gathered in the womb of his mother for forty days as a drop of semen, then it becomes a clinging clot for a similar period, then it becomes a lump of flesh for a similar period. Then the angel is sent, and he breathes the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or blessed. By Him besides whom there is no god, one of you will do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a cubit between him and it, then the Book will overtake him, and he will do the deeds of the people of the Fire and enter it. And one of you will do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only a cubit between him and it, then the Book will overtake him, and he will do the deeds of the people of Paradise and enter it." Al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated it in their two Ṣaḥīḥs. His saying "bikatb" (بكتب) is with the single bāʾ (ب) which is the preposition.

**The Fifth:** From al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both, who said: I memorized from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«دَعْ مَا يُرِيبُكَ إِلَىٰ مَا لَا يُرِيبُكَ»} — "Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt." This is an authentic hadith; Abū ʿĪsā al-Tirmidhī and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Nasāʾī narrated it. Abū ʿĪsā al-Tirmidhī said: "An authentic hadith." His saying "yurībuka" (يُريبك) — with a fatḥah on the first letter and a ḍammah on it — are two dialects, the fatḥah being more famous.

**The Sixth:** From Abū Hurayrah, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ»} — "From the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him." This is a good (ḥasan) hadith; al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah narrated it.

**The Seventh:** From Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ»} — "None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself." Its authenticity is agreed upon.

**The Eighth:** From Abū Hurayrah, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَىٰ أَمَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِمَا أَمَرَ بِهِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ»} — "O people, indeed Allah is Good and accepts only what is good. And indeed Allah the Exalted has commanded the believers with what He commanded the Messengers." He the Exalted said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ»} — "O Messengers, eat from the good things." Then he mentioned a man who undertakes a long journey, disheveled and dusty, stretching his hands towards the sky, saying, "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with the unlawful — so how can he be answered? Muslim narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

**The Ninth:** The hadith of {«لَا ضَرَرَ وَلَا ضِرَارَ»} — "No harm and no reciprocating harm." Mālik narrated it as a mursal (with a broken chain), and al-Dāraquṭnī and a group narrated it from various paths as connected (muttaṣil). It is a good (ḥasan) hadith.
